beforeRecord.q: After a regional downturn ends, one group has suitable job offers but needs time to choose; another cannot meet credentials for expanding occupations. A third group has already accepted paid part-time work while seeking full-time jobs. Which diagnosis respects both cause and official status?
options: The first group is frictionally unemployed, the second structurally unemployed, and the third employed
All three are structurally unemployed because each wants a different job
The first is cyclical, the second frictional, and the third outside the labor force
All three are unemployed until they obtain their preferred full-time jobs
beforeRecord.feedback: Normal matching among suitable jobs is frictional; a persistent credential mismatch is structural. A paid part-time job makes the third group employed under the official measure, even though underemployment may remain.
